name: Blue Men of the Minch

attributes.attribute: swam out to capsize passing ships
passage between the Hebrides and the mainland

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
MacKillop 2008, s.v. Blue Men of the Minch.
text: The Blue Men of the Minch are figures of Scottish maritime folklore. Scots Gaelic names them Na Fir Ghorma, meaning blue men. The Minch runs between the Outer Hebrides and the mainland's Inner Hebrides. Gaelic calls its stream Sruth nam Fear Gorm, the Stream of the Blue Men. They swam out to capsize any ship that crossed. A captain who kept the last word through rhyme could repel them. They moved best around the Shiant Islands in the Hebrides.

okr.objective: Describe the Blue Men of the Minch and their storied channel.
key_results: The Blue Men of the Minch are Scottish maritime folk.
Gaelic calls them Na Fir Ghorma, the blue men.
They toppled passing ships from the channel.
A rhyming captain could keep the last word.
They stayed most active near the Shiant Islands.
